newsitem.title: USA: America Online hit with class action lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: America Online hit with class action lawsuit.

text.p: A California law firm filed a class action lawsuit against America Online Inc. on Thursday, accusing the company of fraudulent business practices.

The lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court here, claims America Online engaged in racketeering, mail fraud and wire fraud. The four plaintiffs, all residents of California, are seeking damages in excess of $100 million.

The lawsuit is the latest in a series of legal attacks against the world's largest online service by frustrated customers who have had trouble logging on to AOL since it went to a flat fee pricing structure of $19.95 a month late last year.

The change from a hour-based fee, sparked a surge in business for the Dulles, Va.-based online provider, straining its capacity to the point where subscribers could not access the service for extended periods of time.

In January, AOL offered to refund customers up to $39.90 each as part of a settlement with 36 states. The company also pledged to hold its membership at 8 million members until it was confident it could meet the needs of its current members.

According to the lawsuit, filed by the Los Angeles law firm of Standbury & Fishelman, AOL executives manipulated its subscriber base in order to run up the company's stock price and achieve a dominant position in the market that would then allow the company to impose higher advertising rates.

The lawsuit also claims AOL used improper methods to retain free trial subscribers and to prevent existing customers from canceling their memberships. These methods included secret payment or allowance of rebates, free hours, refunds, commissions or unearned discounts, the lawsuit claimed.

In the complaint, the law firm claims several AOL executives unloaded large portions of stock before the company announced it was taking a substantial charge to pay for changes in the company's accounting practices.
Earlier, a spokeswoman for AOL said the charges were groundless.
"When the law changes and plaintiffs have to pay for frivolous lawsuits, suits like this won't be filed anymore," she said. "There is no merit to this lawsuit."

In addition to the allegations of mail and wire fraud, the lawsuit charges AOL with violating rights to privacy by failing to prevent outside groups from accessing the computers of subscribers when they make contact with the service.
Lawyers for the plaintiffs said they planned to provide additional details on Friday at a news conference in Los Angeles.
